validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. Intensity Infrastructure Partners LLC and Rainbow Energy Center LLC announced a JV to build a 344-mile ND natural gas pipeline (PGJ, 2025-06-26). Intensity's own site documents the project's actual regulatory-style progression: Phase I open season 2025-02-03 (intensityinfra.com), Phase II Extension open season 2025-04-17 (intensityinfra.com), JV announcement 2025-06-26 (PGJ), and Phase I advanced to a construction decision on executed precedent agreements 2026-01-06 (intensityinfra.com) -- a live, multi-year paper trail from a company with a documented pipeline-construction track record (2,000+ mi built in ND per the 2026-01-06 release), not a one-off GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- 30-in, 208-mi natural gas TRANSMISSION line (intensityinfra.com explicitly: 'natural gas transmission pipeline'; multiple receipt points incl. Northern Border Pipeline and WBI Energy's transmission/storage network, multiple delivery points) feeding Bakken-origin gas east to Casselton -- not a gathering or processing line. DUPLICATE (the cluster question this dispatch flags): P7783 is NOT a duplicate of P7782. They are the sheet's own two phases of ONE project, correctly split: P7782 = Phase I, Watford City->Washburn, 136 mi / 36 in / 1,100 MMcf/d (~1.1M Dth/d); P7783 = this row, Phase II, Washburn->Casselton, 208 mi / 30 in / 430 MMcf/d (~430,000 Dth/d) -- 136+208=344 mi matches the project's own 344-mile headline total (PGJ headline; also the routes-repo PrjName/Miles=344 metadata shared by both PIDs). PGJ states this explicitly as a two-phase build: 'Phase I: 136 miles of 36-inch pipe from near Watford City to Washburn... Phase II: 208 miles of 30-inch pipe from Washburn to Casselton... with capacity of 430,000 Dth/d and multiple delivery points.' Intensity's own 2025-04-17 release states Phase II 'will interconnect with the to-be constructed Phase I pipeline in southern McLean County, North Dakota [Washburn is the McLean County seat], and will terminate near Casselton.' Independent geometric check: the routes-repo geojsons are CONTIGUOUS, not overlapping -- P7782 runs -103.197,47.861 to -101.158,47.379; P7783 (this row) runs -101.234,47.313 to -97.233,46.909 (Casselton, ND is ~46.90N/97.21W, matching the endpoint almost exactly). Both geometries cite the same source PDF (intensityinfra.com/sites/.../IntensityBakkenPhaseII.pdf, an April 2025 project map -- an image PDF, no extractable text, not cited as a [ref] here), which is expected for two segments of one system map, not evidence of double-digitizing. Decreasing diameter (36in->30in) and capacity (1,100->430 MMcf/d) downstream is physically normal for a trunk that delivers gas off along its length (multiple delivery points on Phase II per PGJ) -- not an inconsistency. Verdict: two genuinely distinct, correctly-scoped, contiguous segment rows of one real project; no merge, no relabel.

validity.recommendation: no change recommended; noted for future researchers
validity.researcher_notes: Two minor, non-material sourcing caveats found while reading the documents to exhaustion, neither strong enough to contest the recorded values: (1) StartYear1/StartMonth1=2029/7 is supported by the current PGJ ref ('The target in-service date is July 2029'), but Intensity's own earlier, Phase-II-specific 2025-04-17 release gave a preliminary estimate of 'January 1, 2030' for this segment -- the later PGJ figure (post-JV-finalization) is the better/more current evidence and matches the sheet, so no change is proposed, but a future researcher should not be surprised to find the Jan-2030 figure in older Intensity materials. (2) Capacity=430.00 MMcf/d: the only source stating a Phase-II-specific capacity (PGJ) actually gives '430,000 Dth/d', not MMcf/d -- GEM's CapacityUnits cell reads MMcf/d. Dth/d (MMBtu/d) and Mcf/d are treated as effectively 1:1 in pipeline trade reporting (this same substitution recurs on sibling row P7782's 1,100 MMcf/d vs Intensity's own '1,100,000 Dth/d' Phase I figure), so this is not flagged as a value discrepancy, just a units-label note.
